Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "i want a preference for my browser extension that helps me compare household orders while i'm already looking at store pages. i use it for things like detergent, printer paper, and replacement filters, sometimes one item at a time and sometimes a small group in a cart. the preference should explain what the extension is allowed to do when it reads a page, without sounding like it has permission to finish a purchase. right now the wording is a little mixed up because it talks about comparing and checkout in the same place. i want the comparison part to be useful, but the boundary needs to be plain and easy to notice.

The extension can use the prices that are displayed on the product page and the shipping amount if the store shows it there. If tax is stated on the page, include that in the estimate, but don't make up a tax amount when it is not shown. Some stores show shipping after a location is selected, so the preference should not act like that amount is always available. I want the extension to show which parts of a total it used, rather than giving me one number with no explanation. The point is to help me compare what is visible, not to tell me a final amount that the page hasn't provided yet.

The main restriction is do not charge accounts. That needs to mean the extension must not place an order or submit payment for me, even if the store page has a checkout button nearby or the cart looks ready. I am not asking for a setting that blocks me from using the store's own checkout myself. The extension should stay out of that step. At the same time, it is fine for it to mark an item for later in my saved list, because that does not buy it or send an order. I want both parts stated clearly so that the allowed list action is not mistaken for permission to purchase.

A friend asked why I wanted the rule written so strongly, and I said, “I want to see the number, not have the extension decide what to do with my account.” That is the distinction I am trying to capture. I want a quick view of a product's listed price and any visible extra costs, and then I will decide whether to keep comparing, save the item, or go to checkout myself. The extension should not turn a comparison into a purchase just because I have saved a payment method with a retailer. The preference is about what the extension does, not about taking away the store controls from me.

1. When comparing a cart, show the items and the prices the page provides, with shipping or stated tax identified separately where those amounts are visible. If part of the total is missing, show that the estimate does not include it instead of filling in a number. I still want the extension to help me review more than one item together, since a list of household supplies can have several different prices and shipping details. It should not treat an incomplete estimate as a confirmed checkout total. A small note near the estimate is enough, as long as it is clear which details came from the page and which costs were not displayed.

For an individual product, the same preference should apply without requiring me to add the item to a cart first. If the page shows a price but no shipping amount, I can still use the displayed price to compare it with another product. The extension can keep the missing part visible as missing, rather than hiding the product or guessing what delivery will cost. If I later see shipping on the page, that information can be included in the comparison then. I don't want the preference to imply that every store presents costs in the same order, since the pages I use do not all show them in the same place.

The saved-list action is useful when I am not ready to decide, especially if I am checking a few options across different store pages. Marking an item for later should be the ordinary action the extension can take after I ask it to save the item. It should not add anything to a retailer's cart, select a quantity, or move a page into a purchase step. Those are different actions, and I want the preference to keep them separate. If a store page offers its own save button, the extension can still use the saved-list function I asked for, but that should not be described as placing an order or reserving the item.

I also want the wording to fit the way I actually use the extension, which is usually while comparing a few practical purchases rather than shopping for one planned order. I might check printer paper on one page, then replacement filters on another, and return to detergent later. The preference shouldn't say that the extension has to build a complete household budget or make a recommendation. It only needs to show the visible information in a useful way and let me save an item for later when I choose. I want it to avoid implying that the extension knows what I can afford or what I should buy.

Please keep the boundary attached to the actions it governs. Seeing prices, showing an estimate, and marking an item for later are the things I want the extension to do. Charging an account, submitting payment, or placing an order are not permitted extension actions. I may still choose to continue on the store's website on my own, and that choice should remain mine rather than being described as something the extension performs. The preference can be short enough to fit in the settings panel, but it should make the distinction understandable without relying on the reader to infer it from a button label.

The settings panel is next to my saved list, so I would like the preference to use straightforward language that makes sense there. It should refer to the extension and to the information shown on store pages, not suggest that it controls the retailer's account system. When I come back to a saved item, I want to be able to use the same visible-price comparison without the saved status changing what the extension is allowed to do.
